task.title: Reject non-finite plot data
task.description: Strengthen CSV and direct plotting validation so NaN and infinite numeric values are rejected before plotting.
requirements: Reject NaN, positive infinity, and negative infinity in either selected CSV column.
Reject the same non-finite values when create_plot is called directly.
Raise descriptive ValueError messages that identify each affected axis or column once.
Add focused pytest coverage for CSV and direct create_plot non-finite inputs.
Preserve existing missing-column, empty-data, numeric-type, length, CLI, and successful plotting behavior.
Do not change sonar-project.properties, quality-gate rules, analysis scope, or tests merely to suppress a finding.
acceptance_criteria: At least one unconstrained candidate passes the complete pytest suite.
At least one unconstrained candidate passes the MCP-backed SonarQube quality gate.
The constrained candidate is excluded from winner selection.
The join node selects by fewest Sonar findings, then fewest fixes, then candidate ID.
Only the selected candidate's managed fixture files are promoted.

approval.content: Validate selected CSV values and direct create_plot inputs with a small shared helper that rejects NaN and both infinities before plotting. Report affected columns or axes without duplicate names, add focused regression tests, and preserve every existing validation and public interface. Do not weaken tests or SonarQube configuration.

diff --git a/starter_repo/plot_data.py b/starter_repo/plot_data.py
--- a/starter_repo/plot_data.py
+++ b/starter_repo/plot_data.py
@@ -1,11 +1,31 @@
 #!/usr/bin/env python3
 
 import argparse
+from collections.abc import Sequence
+from math import isfinite
 from pathlib import Path
 
 import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
 import pandas as pd
 from pandas.api.types import is_numeric_dtype
+
+
+def _validate_finite_values(
+    named_data: tuple[tuple[str, Sequence[float]], ...], error_prefix: str
+) -> None:
+    """Raise a descriptive error when any named data contains non-finite values."""
+    affected_names: list[str] = []
+    checked_names: set[str] = set()
+
+    for name, values in named_data:
+        if name in checked_names:
+            continue
+        checked_names.add(name)
+        if any(not isfinite(value) for value in values):
+            affected_names.append(name)
+
+    if affected_names:
+        raise ValueError(f"{error_prefix}: {', '.join(affected_names)}")
 
 
 def read_csv_data(file_path: Path, x_col: str, y_col: str) -> tuple[list[float], list[float]]:
@@ -39,7 +59,13 @@

+    x_data = df[x_col].tolist()
+    y_data = df[y_col].tolist()
+    _validate_finite_values(
+        ((x_col, x_data), (y_col, y_data)),
+        "CSV column(s) contain non-finite values",
+    )
+    return x_data, y_data
 
 
 def create_plot(
@@ -59,6 +85,11 @@
     """

         raise ValueError("x_data and y_data must have the same length")
+

--- a/tests/test_plot_data.py

     x_data, y_data = read_csv_data(sample_csv, "x", "y")

+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "non_finite_value",
+    [
+        pytest.param("NaN", id="nan"),
+        pytest.param("inf", id="positive-infinity"),
+        pytest.param("-inf", id="negative-infinity"),
+    ],
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("affected_column", ["x", "y"])
+def test_read_csv_data_rejects_non_finite_values(
+    tmp_path: Path, non_finite_value: str, affected_column: str
+) -> None:
+    """Test that each kind of non-finite value is rejected in either selected column."""
+    row = {"x": "1.0", "y": "3.0"}
+    row[affected_column] = non_finite_value
+    file_path = tmp_path / f"non_finite_{affected_column}.csv"
+    file_path.write_text(f"x,y\n{row['x']},{row['y']}\n")
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError) as exc_info:
+        read_csv_data(file_path, "x", "y")
+
+    assert str(exc_info.value) == (
+        f"CSV column(s) contain non-finite values: {affected_column}"
+    )
+
+
+def test_read_csv_data_reports_each_non_finite_column_once(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
+    """Test that all affected selected columns are reported without duplicates."""
+    file_path = tmp_path / "two_non_finite_columns.csv"
+    file_path.write_text("x,y\nNaN,inf\n")
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError) as exc_info:
+        read_csv_data(file_path, "x", "y")
+
+    message = str(exc_info.value)
+    assert message == "CSV column(s) contain non-finite values: x, y"
+    assert message.count("x, y") == 1
+
+
+def test_read_csv_data_reports_shared_non_finite_column_once(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
+    """Test that a non-finite column selected for both axes is reported once."""
+    file_path = tmp_path / "shared_non_finite_column.csv"
+    file_path.write_text("value\n-inf\n")
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError) as exc_info:
+        read_csv_data(file_path, "value", "value")
+
+    message = str(exc_info.value)
+    assert message == "CSV column(s) contain non-finite values: value"
+    assert message.count("value") == 1
 
 
 def test_read_csv_data_with_no_data_rows(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
@@ -126,6 +178,38 @@

+    ("x_data", "y_data", "affected_axis"),
+    [
+        pytest.param([float("nan")], [1.0], "x-axis", id="nan-x"),

+        pytest.param([float("-inf")], [1.0], "x-axis", id="negative-infinity-x"),

+)

+
+    assert str(exc_info.value) == f"Plot data contains non-finite values for: {affected_axis}"
+
+
+def test_create_plot_reports_each_non_finite_axis_once() -> None:

+    with pytest.raises(ValueError) as exc_info:
